messages:
carla_support: Customer T-471 reporting intermittent SSE disconnects with partial payloads, then they get charged for full-response tokens. Happening ~20% of streams from EU region behind our customer’s corp-proxy. Logs show server-side write errors right before disconnect. :frowning:

alice_infra: ugh. any specific error lines from the runtime?

carla_support: pasted snippets from their support bundle:

```
2026-03-01T09:12:33Z ERROR stream_write: write failed errno=11 (EAGAIN) client_id=abc123 conn_fd=56
2026-03-01T09:12:35Z WARN connection_close: aborting stream due to write failure: write returned -1 (Broken pipe)
```

ben_sre: errno=11 is EAGAIN (non-blocking) — indicates send buffer full and the kernel would block. Then server tries and sees EAGAIN and we fall back to abort? We should not immediately abort on EAGAIN. What does our write path do?

alice_infra: our current path attempts one non-blocking write, logs and tears down if it doesn't complete within X ms. That was intentional to avoid stuck goroutines from very slow clients. But maybe too aggressive for corp proxies that buffer slowly.

dave_net: corp proxies often have tiny TCP receive windows and add buffering which can cause backpressure. Also some proxies (older F5/NGINX configs) enable large proxy_buffering which reads upstream aggressively then slows down to client — intermediate buffering can trigger burst billing.

carla_support: customer says their proxy is nginx 1.18 with default proxy_buffering=on and proxy_buffers 8 4k. They tested with their app and saw gaps followed by 502s. Billing team flagged a spike in token usage because client retried and got duplicate partial responses.

ben_sre: useful repro: simulate a slow consumer with netcat. On the server: `./simple-sse-server` (our test binary) streaming 1 msg/sec. On client test machine run: `nc -l 9001 | while read -r line; do sleep 0.75; printf "%s\n" "$line"; done` — that forces the accept->read side to slow. We repro EAGAIN quickly. Suggest we add exponential retry on EAGAIN with small backoff before hard-abort.

alice_infra: agree. Also add a header we can set for proxies: `X-Accel-Buffering: no` (nginx) or `Cache-Control: no-transform` and ensure Transfer-Encoding: chunked present. For customers behind proxies that buffer, recommend disabling proxy_buffering for SSE endpoints.

carla_support: customer asked for a minimal workaround they can apply without infra changes. Any on-client suggestions?

ben_sre: client side: set HTTP request header `Connection: keep-alive`, disable HTTP client buffers (in some mobile libs, enable streaming mode), and periodically read socket to drain. But more realistic: increase our server send buffer so a slow reader doesn't make us EAGAIN on first small flush. E.g. setsockopt SO_SNDBUF to 256k-1M.

dave_net: also check TCP_NODELAY; for SSE small writes, Nagle can batch causing perceived stalls. Enabling TCP_NODELAY on both sides helps low-latency writes.

carla_support: any quick config snippets we can share with the customer?

alice_infra: paste for nginx:

```
location /v1/stream {
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_cache off;
  proxy_set_header X-Accel-Buffering off;
}
```
and on server side (go example):

```
// before accept loop
tcpListener, _ := net.Listen("tcp", ":8080")
// set OS-level send buffer
// NOTE: requires syscall / raw conn in go, shown conceptually
setsockopt(tcpConn.FD(), SOL_SOCKET, SO_SNDBUF, 262144)
```

ben_sre: for our runtime change proposal: 1) on EAGAIN, do 3 retry attempts with backoff 50ms->200ms while keeping per-stream deadline; 2) expose `stream.send_sndbuf` in config for Dedicated/Private; 3) add metric `stream.write_backpressure_retries` and alert if high.

carla_support: customer also worried about billing duplicates — any mitigation server-side?

alice_infra: we can add idempotent stream markers: if a client reconnects quickly and provides `Last-Event-ID` or our `x-rw-stream-id`, we can resume rather than re-emit tokens. Longer term: billing should only charge for committed tokens; we can flag partial-abort events and do a support credit if duplication detected.

monitor-bot: alert: eu-streams.write_eagain.count spike at 2026-03-01T09:00-09:20 (see dashboard link) :eyes:

ben_sre: ok next steps: 1) send customer quick nginx snippet + suggestion to enable `curl --no-buffer` test and netcat slow-reader repro; 2) patch runtime to retry EAGAIN as safe rollback; 3) add metric & alert; 4) follow up on billing duplicates with finance. I'll open a PR for runtime patch and config toggle.

carla_support: thanks — I'll send customer the nginx snippet + a short repro they can run and offer an interim credit if they can show duplicated token charges.

alice_infra: FYI I'll add a small doc to devex about SSE best-practices behind proxies.

carla_support: tagging @dave_net for visibility. :wave:
